t: Missing Value Handler - Signature build-tool concept
title: Missing Value Handler - Signature build-tool concept
definition: Identifies and handles absent data according to explicit rules.
description:
Missing Value Handler is the Signature build-tool concept that identifies and handles absent data according to explicit rules. In the Signature line, it is not a loose collection of scripts but a deterministic capability: the same build request produces the same verified result on every run, on every machine. This database documents the concept in full - what it is, the seven framework pillars that implement it, the real techniques it stands on, the standards it honors, and laddered drills that teach it from first principles to compounded mastery.

An AI that builds on demand needs Missing Value Handler the way a workshop needs its central bench. Without it, every build becomes improvisation: requirements drift, steps run out of order, and nobody can say why a result came out the way it did. With it, the build becomes a protocol - inputs declared, transformations explicit, outputs checked against the original request. That protocol is what these records describe, pillar by pillar.

Every record in this database carries a runnable demonstration program, because a build tool that cannot show its work cannot be trusted with real work. Read the overview, study the pillars, practice the drills, and run the demos: by the end the Missing Value Handler will be a capability you can invoke, not a concept you have read about.

t: Signature Scrubber - Missing Value Handler framework pillar
title: Signature Scrubber - Missing Value Handler framework pillar
definition: The Scrubber component of the Signature Missing Value Handler framework, owning scrubber. Signature concept.
description:
The Scrubber is a load-bearing component of the Signature Missing Value Handler framework. Its contract is narrow and absolute: within the framework, everything concerning the framework's scrubber responsibilities belongs to the Scrubber, and the Scrubber answers for it. This separation is what makes the framework testable - the Scrubber can be exercised alone, with declared inputs and checkable outputs, long before it is wired into a full build.

In operation the Scrubber works like this. A build request arrives carrying the Missing Value Handler charter (identifies and handles absent data according to explicit rules.). The Scrubber reads its portion of the charter, performs its transformation, and hands a verified intermediate result to the next pillar. If its checks fail, it stops the line and reports exactly what was wrong, instead of passing corruption downstream. That fail-fast discipline is the Signature line's signature.

Signature-concept illustration: a builder asks for a small dataclean job that needs Missing Value Handler. The Scrubber takes the request's scrubber responsibilities slice, applies the framework's deterministic procedure, and returns its result with a proof of what it did. Run this record's demo program to see the Scrubber's core logic execute on a concrete example - the same logic, the same result, every run.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for Missing Value Handler. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Deduper - Missing Value Handler framework pillar
title: Signature Deduper - Missing Value Handler framework pillar
definition: The Deduper component of the Signature Missing Value Handler framework, owning deduper. Signature concept.
description:
Inside the Signature Missing Value Handler framework, the Deduper owns the framework's deduper responsibilities. Frameworks fail when responsibilities blur; the Signature line prevents that by giving each pillar a written contract, and the Deduper's contract is the sharpest of the seven. It accepts declared inputs, applies one deterministic transformation, and emits a result that any other pillar - or any auditor - can verify independently.

What distinguishes the Signature Deduper from an ad-hoc script is the verification loop. Every execution is checked against the charter (Identifies and handles absent data according to explicit rules.). If the result cannot be justified against the charter, it is rejected and the build halts with a diagnostic instead of a silent wrong answer. Deterministic builds are not a slogan here; they are the acceptance test.

Walk through it concretely. A Data cleaning and transformation build needs Missing Value Handler, so the framework invokes the Deduper on the the framework's deduper responsibilities portion of the work. The demo program attached to this record executes the pillar's essential algorithm on sample data - run it with node and watch each step print its reasoning. Same seed, same output: that reproducibility is the entire point.

t: Signature Imputer - Missing Value Handler framework pillar
title: Signature Imputer - Missing Value Handler framework pillar
definition: The Imputer component of the Signature Missing Value Handler framework, owning imputer. Signature concept.
description:
The Signature Missing Value Handler framework decomposes the capability (Identifies and handles absent data according to explicit rules.) into seven pillars, and the Imputer is the one that owns the framework's imputer responsibilities. Owning a responsibility means three things in the Signature line: the pillar declares exactly what it accepts, it publishes exactly what it guarantees, and it logs enough evidence that a third party can replay its work and reach the same conclusion.

This discipline pays off when builds go wrong, because they always eventually do. When a Missing Value Handler result looks suspicious, the auditor does not re-run the whole build and hope; they replay the Imputer's log, check its guarantees against its inputs, and find the fault at its source. The pillar is thus both a worker and a witness - it does the work and it testifies about the work.

Try it yourself: this record's demo runs the Imputer's core procedure on a worked example. The program is plain JavaScript - save it as demo.js and run it with node, or press Run in the Demo Lab. Change the inputs and re-run; the procedure is deterministic, so you can verify every claim the description makes.
